source.title: Batch Normalization with Enhanced Linear Transformation
source.authors: Yuhui Xu; Ling-Xi Xie; Cihang Xie; Jie-Ru Mei; Siyuan Qiao; Wei Shen; H. Xiong; A. Yuille

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares BNET, an enhanced batch-normalization module, with standard BN and reports faster training curves. It does not test the listed versions’ central comparisons, such as BN versus no normalization, or whether training reaches near-zero classification error.
record.gate_note: The paper reports faster training loss decline for BNET than BN on ImageNet and MS-COCO, but does not report numerical training-error results or compare BN with a network without normalization. These results are recorded as findings outside the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The study uses batch normalization and evaluates its proposed BNET enhancement against standard BN. These comparisons do not test V6's BN versus no-normalization comparison or Fixup equivalence. Its own results do not test V1–V5 either.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors report consistent recognition accuracy gains and faster convergence with BNET compared with BN, with small additional computational costs. Their proposed explanation involving enhanced spatial cues is a conjecture.
record.recipe_differences: The study replaces BN’s per-channel linear transformation with a channel-wise convolution (BNET-k); it does not compare BN with no normalization.
record.method_sensitivity: Training convergence is reported for the Auto-Augment condition and the MS-COCO detection setting as well as ImageNet without Auto-Augment; the text describes faster loss decline in each.

fits_no_version.finding: BNET-3 is reported to accelerate convergence relative to standard BN on ImageNet, with and without Auto-Augment, and on MS-COCO detection.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Enhancing BN's affine transformation with neighboring spatial responses can accelerate training convergence compared with standard BN in the tested settings.

record.problems: Training-curve findings are described qualitatively without numerical loss values or uncertainty estimates. The paper does not report a direct comparison of BN with no normalization for these findings.
record.rows_left_out: No additional training-curve results meeting the row criteria were identified.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, including random or corrupted labels, and its dependence on capacity, stopping, and regularization.
Spurious local minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and their dependence on extra student neurons.
Training degradation with plain-network depth, prevention by identity shortcuts, and the stated initialization exceptions.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, learning speed, and trainable depth.
Recovery or divergence relative to learning-rate stability thresholds and curvature evolution.
Training speed and learning-rate tolerance with BN versus the same networks without normalization, and comparable training using Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The corrected states concern whether the rows establish a listed version; they do not dispute the reported BNET convergence gains. Qualitative convergence evidence is sufficient for the outside-version finding. The decisive mismatch is the comparison being tested.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, random or corrupted labels, model size, optimizer, and training duration effects.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual network depth effects and shortcut comparisons.
Initialization choices, signal propagation, and trainable depth.
Learning rates above stability limits, curvature, and divergence.
BN versus the same networks without BN, and Fixup without normalization.

rows.subject: ResNet-50 (BNET-3)
rows.operation_detail: Compared training curves after replacing BN with BNET-3.
rows.value: The model using BNET converges faster than the model using BN.
rows.note: The text describes the training curves but gives no numerical training-loss values.
rows.check: This is the proposed method's performance against BN, outside the listed versions. Faster convergence is explicitly reported, but cannot establish the effect of adding BN versus no normalization.

rows.subject: ResNet-50 (BNET-3)
rows.operation_detail: Compared training curves after replacing BN with BNET-3.
rows.value: With the benefit of BNET, the loss drops more sharply compared with BN.
rows.note: The text describes the curve comparison but gives no numerical training-loss values.
rows.check: This is the proposed method's performance against BN under Auto-Augment, outside the listed versions. Sharper loss decline does not establish any listed version.

rows.subject: Faster R-CNN with ResNet-50 backbone (BNET-3)
rows.operation_detail: Compared training curves after replacing BN with BNET-3.
rows.value: The training loss of the model with BNET declines sharply.
rows.note: The figure is described qualitatively; no numerical loss values are given.
rows.check: This is the proposed method's detection training trajectory against BN, outside the listed versions. Add that backbones are pretrained on ImageNet and BN statistics are frozen; this is not a BN versus no-normalization experiment.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
